state.case_summary:
A 50-year-old male patient was brought to the emergency department due to syncope 30 minutes before admission. The patient reported experiencing palpitation and amaurosis, followed by loss of consciousness that lasted for several minutes, without any preceding body position change, cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath. The patient experienced a previous episode of syncope 1 month prior. Medical history indicated only diabetes, which was well controlled with medication.

Patient was alert and asymptomatic, with vital signs: blood pressure 125/96 mm Hg, pulse rate 81 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 99% under ambient air. Physical examination showed normal results.

- Laboratory Tests: Blood glucose, electrolytes, D-dimer, troponin I (<0.01 ng/mL), and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide were normal.- Cardiac Tests:  - Electrocardiogram: Initially normal  - Transthoracic echocardiography: Normal, with left ventricular ejection fraction of 58%  - 12-lead 24-hour Holter monitoring: Recorded polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during presyncope episode, with QTc of 403 milliseconds    Image Title: 12-Lead Holter Monitoring    Image Description: ST-segment elevation and fusion with R waves in leads I, aVL, and V1 to V5, followed by short bursts of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia- Coronary Angiography:   - 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD  - 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery  - Intravascular ultrasonography showed minimum lumen area of 5.92 mm2 in proximal LAD, with plaque burden of 74%
